Hereditary motor peripheral neuropathy; muscle wasting is neurogenic. Cardiomyopathy occurs in 1/5, below threshold.
Autoimmune neuromuscular-junction disease; generalized weakness reflects impaired transmission rather than primary muscle damage.
Hereditary autonomic neuropathy causing abnormal sweating and thermoregulation; sweating alone does not establish skin damage.
Structural narrowing of the lacrimal drainage apparatus.
Autoimmune endocrine failure and defining oral candidiasis; nail dystrophy ~49% and alopecia ~36%. Ocular disease reported at 30-79% omitted under cap.
Protozoal infection directly involving intestinal epithelium.
Glomerular podocyte injury and segmental sclerosis; heterogeneous causes do not establish an immune mechanism across the group.

Bartonella infection invades erythrocytes with hemolytic anemia; the supplied Carrion disease definition also includes defining chronic cutaneous proliferations.
Congenital ocular motility disorder caused by absent or aberrant abducens-nerve innervation.
Variable mosaic Edwards phenotype with neurodevelopmental impairment and characteristic limb malformations; cardiac frequency is insufficiently certain for inclusion.
Juvenile open-angle glaucoma damages the optic nerve, included in the ocular axis.
Defining developmental disability; skeletal abnormalities commonly reported: brachydactyly 3/3, kyphoscoliosis and foot deformities 2/2. Cardiac/urinary frequency unclear.
Defining congenital finger and toe malformations with contractures and ankylosis.
Placental implantation disorder is obstetric; bleeding does not make this a primary blood or coagulation disease.
Congenital joint contractures with hypertonia 5/5 and tremor 4/4; ocular motility impairment/strabismus reported in 4/4. Other organ findings are isolated reports.
Umbrella disorder defined by abnormal pigmentation of the skin; syndromic complications do not apply across the group.
Psychiatric trauma-related disorder without qualifying direct organ damage.
Congenital urethral opening malformation; the urethra belongs to the renal axis despite the reproductive-system parent.
Carcinoma predominantly arising in the nasopharynx, included in the pulmonary axis; rare alternative primary sites do not define the umbrella.
Cerebral white-matter disease with subcortical cysts, seizures and progressive motor/cognitive deterioration; dysphagia is neurologic.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting limb bones, epiphyses and spine; small or broad nails alone do not establish additional tissue damage.
Benign epidermal keratinocytic neoplasm of vulvar skin; the supplied definition establishes a skin lesion despite misleading carcinoma parents.
Characteristic cutaneous/oral hamartomas and GI hamartomatous polyposis; benign thyroid structural lesions occur in roughly 50-70%. Cancer risks are excluded.
